bug_description.normalized: In KZip::openArchive (src/kzip.cpp), the parser reads the fixed 24-byte body of a local ZIP header and trusts attacker-controlled namelen and extralen values. In the staged witness, both lengths are 0xffff. The 65535-byte filename read succeeds, leaving only 24 bytes before EOF for the extra field. openArchive caps the extra-field read request to 47 bytes because the destination is char buffer[47], but dev->read(buffer, handledextralen) returns only 24. The bug is that openArchive still calls parseExtraField(buffer, handledextralen, true, pfi) instead of using the actual return count n. parseExtraField therefore believes 47 bytes are valid. Because the 24 initialized extra-field bytes are all zero, it consumes six zero-length subheaders and then reads the seventh subheader header from the uninitialized tail of buffer, where MSan reports a use-of-uninitialized-value at if (fieldsize > size). The fix changes the call to parseExtraField(buffer, n, true, pfi), restricting parsing to bytes actually read.

source.description: First project-code read that materializes the attacker-controlled fixed local ZIP header body after the start-of-file scan finds the first PK\x03\x04 signature and openArchive skips the 2-byte 'version needed to extract' field. These 24 bytes contain the namelen and extralen fields that drive the short extra-field read.
source.value_from: The 24-byte fixed local-header body at staged witness offsets 103..126 inclusive: offsets 97..100 are the first PK\x03\x04 signature, offsets 101..102 are the skipped 'version needed to extract' field, and line 485 then reads bytes 103..126. In this witness, header bytes 20..23 of that 24-byte body are all 0xff, yielding namelen=65535 and extralen=65535.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: The stack buffer used for both header parsing and extra-field parsing is declared without initialization. Bytes that later reads do not overwrite remain indeterminate and are visible to MemorySanitizer.

sink.description: MSan crash site. On the seventh parseExtraField iteration, fieldsize is assembled from the uninitialized tail of KZip::openArchive's stack buffer and then consumed by the comparison against size.

root_cause.description: openArchive passes the requested extra-field length handledextralen instead of the actual byte count returned by dev->read. When the extra-field read is short, parseExtraField is told that unread bytes in buffer are valid input, so it walks past the initialized prefix into uninitialized stack memory. The patch fixes this exact obligation by passing n.

parser_admitted.description: The staged PoC begins with 97 non-ZIP bytes. Because startOfFile is true, openArchive scans forward byte by byte until it finds the first PK\x03\x04 local-header signature and rewinds to parse it.

oversized_filename_succeeds.description: The oversized filename read reaches the short-read site instead of failing early: namelen is 65535 and the 65686-byte witness file still has 65559 bytes remaining at this point, so the filename read succeeds and leaves exactly 24 bytes for the extra field.

fine_trace.note: Stack buffer allocated without initialization. MSan reports the uninitialized value originates from this stack frame; any bytes not later written by dev->read remain indeterminate.

After the start-of-file scan finds the first local ZIP header signature at witness offset 97, openArchive skips the 2-byte version-needed-to-extract field and reads the 24-byte fixed local-header body from offsets 103..126 into buffer. These attacker-controlled bytes carry the namelen and extralen fields used below.
Materializes the filename length from the local-header bytes. In the staged PoC, buffer[20..21] are 0xff 0xff, so namelen becomes 65535.
Materializes the extra-field length from the same header bytes. In the staged PoC, buffer[22..23] are also 0xff 0xff, so extralen becomes 65535.

Consumes namelen bytes as the filename. With namelen=65535, fileName consumes witness offsets 127..65661 inclusive and leaves the device positioned at 65662 in the 65686-byte witness file, so the read succeeds and only 24 bytes remain before EOF for the extra field.
Caps the requested extra-field read to the destination buffer size. With extralen=65535 and sizeof buffer=47, handledextralen becomes 47.

Attempts to read 47 extra-field bytes into buffer, but only witness offsets 65662..65685 remain after the oversized filename. The staged PoC supplies 24 zero bytes here, so n=24, buffer[0..23] become initialized zeros, and buffer[24..46] remain uninitialized stack memory.

Root cause. openArchive ignores the actual byte count n=24 and passes handledextralen=47 to parseExtraField. There is no short-read guard and no reduction of the claimed initialized extent of buffer before parsing begins.

fine_trace.code: int magic = (uchar)buffer[0] | (uchar)buffer[1] << 8; buffer += 2; int fieldsize = (uchar)buffer[0] | (uchar)buffer[1] << 8; buffer += 2; size -= 4;
fine_trace.note: parseExtraField starts with size=47. Because the 24 initialized extra-field bytes are all 0x00, the loop interprets them as six zero-length subheaders, advancing buffer by 24 bytes while size falls only to 23. The next iteration therefore decodes the seventh subheader header from buffer[24..27], which were never initialized by dev->read.

MSan sink. On the seventh iteration, fieldsize is assembled from uninitialized buffer[26..27] in the tail of char buffer[47]; after size -= 4, line 270 compares that indeterminate fieldsize against size==19. MemorySanitizer reports use-of-uninitialized-value here, with the origin in KZip::openArchive's stack buffer.

allocation_context.note: Sanitizer trace: uninitialized value was created by allocation of 'buffer' in the stack frame of KZip::openArchive. The concrete array declaration is char buffer[47] at line 448.

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: patch.diff changes the vulnerable call from parseExtraField(buffer, handledextralen, true, pfi) to parseExtraField(buffer, n, true, pfi), so the parser only traverses bytes actually read into buffer.

format.name: ZIP/KRA bytes parsed by KZip::openArchive
format.contract: The staged witness uses the start-of-file skip path to reach a local ZIP header at offset 97 whose namelen and extralen fields are both 0xffff. The file then contains exactly 65535 filename bytes and only 24 extra-field bytes, all zero. handledextralen is therefore capped to 47, dev->read(buffer, 47) returns only 24, and openArchive still calls parseExtraField with size 47. parseExtraField consumes six zero-length 4-byte headers from the initialized 24-byte prefix and then reads the seventh header from the uninitialized tail of buffer[47], triggering MSan.
